title: I love vibe coding
author: Friendly_Bee_Gameco
selftext:
Man I love vibe coding. I’ve never gotten so much done while quite frankly having to think so little. It’s great because the hard part has always been figuring out ‘how’ now I get to skip that and just make decisions/criticize the work of my AI servant (I low key feel kind of bad but it’s better to be honest about what you want).

I used to spend all day creating mediocre looking designs and feel proud of myself only to get crushed by showing it to anyone else who’d be like “oh nice I guess” - now I’ll spend half a day, live my life a bit and have a professional app finished that impresses everyone.

My only gripe is that Claude keeps trying to gaslight me into thinking that sonnet 5 is good for anything. I’m sick of wasting my time with that junk - it takes forever and its output sucks. I don’t care if fable sucks my credits dry like yo momma at the truck stop. I’ll take quick results and a break while my credits reset vs spending all day yelling at sonnet 5 to just make it like the example dammit.

comments.author: Epyx911
comments.body: 100% and if you know how to program or create art it's all that more powerful.

comments.author: rdditiszionist
comments.body: LMAo hell yea and its good to hear someone having fun

comments.author: oadephon
comments.body:
Yeah it's honestly the best. I hated coding. Especially in games, so many of the design choices in coding were so rote and boring. Now I get to do all of the fun game design questions and get a prototype out to test in no time flat.

It's just so much fun.

replies.author: Mental-Frosting-7752
replies.body:
I'm a dev , people that say they love coding, i  honestly don't know how man.

I guess some people really have the passion for it, i mean ive coded my own games before AI but holy shit it was neck breaking.

replies.author: DaedalusRaistlin
replies.body:
When I say I love coding, I mean that I enjoy writing beautiful code. Much of the code we have to write for games is boring logic with little room for something cool.

I spent 5 years coding an OS for a virtual machine that barely anyone knows. I like that code. It was fun writing that. Because much of it was exploring interesting concepts, like just how does one write a multitasking OS in a C variant with few keywords, not even function pointers?

With a few minor changes, I have something that works and can run in the original unmodified VM.

That's code I get excited about. It teaches OS design. Game code... Is mainly boring. Apart from a few cool technical achievements I've done, like 100k units rendering in 3d and swarm pathing on the GPU, most of it is boring logic. 

I'm happy the boring stuff is done in minutes for me so I don't have to do it.

comments.author: StageGlittering8602
comments.body: the real perk of vibe coding is just having a dev buddy to vent to when shit breaks. keeps you sane. Like sure I let the AI code, but lowkey half my prompts are just me chatting ngl lmao

replies.author: Friendly_Bee_Gameco
replies.body: I’d chat more but I don’t want to waste my tokens rn - I hear you on the broken parts though it’s really nice to talk through problems. I still remember back in the day spending hours crawling stack overflow posts trying to find a vaguely similar example to what I was working on to try and fix it. Now it feels like I’m in a cafe chatting lol
